summary: Restored the Node-wrapper question to an execution-backed account on a conforming prefix. CheckRun 4dc33f26f12e4cd69f7aae09af6c1ee6 (fixed experiment c3dd9a52a0c44b21af5b3204cf642efb-experiment, version 2, whose pump persists each Ready's entries, hard state and snapshots before sending and advancing) parsed five events with no loss and resolved all six comparisons: the two controls hold (parsed index 1 - before the removal Propose returns no error in 0ms and the leader's log index is 2, so a follower's proposal is forwarded to the group), both premises hold on the witness event (index 4 - the leader's configuration contains node 2 again and the node still knows leader 1 in the same term), and both witness assertions are violated (index 4 - Propose returns only when its 300ms deadline fires and the leader's log index stays at 4). The event stream also shows the conforming sequence (applied/committed 1, 2, 3, 4 as the configuration moves voters=(1 2) to voters=(1) and back), which is what the earlier receipt's prefix lacked. The conclusion therefore returns from conditional to violated with the defect claim asserted, the earlier receipt 8b3e88d4b4a641fa8ddc723ecc0ba56d is kept in history but withdrawn as evidence for the witness (its prefix omitted the persistence duty), and joint_history records why the two receipts are comparable and which one is relied upon. Counterevidence keeps the holding controls, the documented proposal-loss caveat and the supersession relation; limitations keep the one-sided wrapper harness, the 300ms deadline, the still-unmeasured leadership-change restore path (the diagnostic block hung the run and was removed) and the open question of the wrapper's intended semantics for a re-added node.
